findings.title: FMEA H-6 still gives the superseded J400 bench-ramp window (turn-off 4.5-4.8 V, turn-on 4.9-5.2 V); the round 24 fix (R24-TRI-03 / D-R24-19) corrected the other records but not this one
contradicts: docs/ORDERING.md 8.3 J400 ESD bullet, line 648: "expect turn-off 4.29-4.80 V and turn-on 4.72-5.25 V (nominal 4.51 / 4.96 V; Calculation over TI SLVSFC9C p9's thresholds, 1 % resistors, +/-0.1 uA EN leakage and D402 <= 50 nA, R24-TRI-03, D-R24-19)"; the same window in REQUIREMENTS F9 (line 63), M3_R10 (line 376) and the battery_entry.kicad_sch C87 note ("on at 4.72-5.25 V and off at 4.29-4.80 V")

TI TPS25947 SLVSFC9C p9 (https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps25947.pdf): VUVLO(R) 1.183-1.223 V, VUVLO(F) 1.076-1.116 V, IENLKG -0.1 to 0.1 uA; Infineon ESD103-B1-02 Rev 1.3 Table 3 p5: IR <= 50 nA at 15 V
STATUS.md line 16: "the generated EN text and every record carry D402's leakage, the corrected bench-ramp window (off 4.29-4.80 V, on 4.72-5.25 V) and the 18 % chatter line"

evidence.statement: docs/FMEA_REDUNDANCY.md line 36, H-6 / V-18 row of the "R10 applicability" current-disposition table: "After a suspected discharge, repeat the bench supply ramp (turn-off 4.5-4.8 V, turn-on 4.9-5.2 V) with the switch-off and J121.2 checks."
evidence.calculation: J400 closed: V_pack = VT x (R80+R165+R81)/R81 + I_EN x (R80+R165) + I_D402 x R80, over 1 % parts, TI thresholds, +/-0.1 uA and D402 0-50 nA (.supervisor/r25_safety/en_model.py, en_model.out): turn-off 4.2876-4.8021 V (nominal 4.5053 V), turn-on 4.7233-5.2512 V (nominal 4.960 V). The FMEA window rejects healthy boards that turn off at 4.29-4.50 V (the nominal 4.505 V sits on its edge) or turn on at 4.72-4.90 V or 5.20-5.25 V.
evidence.history: R24-SAFETY-03 (round24_safety.json) listed FMEA H-6 l.36 and named it in its fix; R24-TRI-03 narrowed the fix to ORDERING 8.3, REQUIREMENTS F9, M3_R10 and the sheet note, and commit c4bb56b changed only H-6's BAT_FAULT_N clause (git show c4bb56b --stat: FMEA 1 line). The R24-TRI-03 disposition row (R10_VALIDATION line 2074) lists only those three records; STATUS line 16 says "every record".

findings.impact: AGENTS section 1 points to FMEA H-6 for pad arming (row "Pad arming access in flight configuration (FMEA H-6, V-18)"). Applied after a suspected discharge, its window can judge a healthy board EN-damaged, so the post-event check cannot be carried out correctly from this record, and STATUS's "every record" statement is false while it stands. No fire consequence: the 4.80 V upper turn-off edge that screens extra EN leakage to GND is the same in both windows.
findings.concrete_fix: Text only. In FMEA H-6 replace "(turn-off 4.5-4.8 V, turn-on 4.9-5.2 V)" with "(turn-off 4.29-4.80 V, turn-on 4.72-5.25 V, nominal 4.51 / 4.96 V; ORDERING 8.3, D-R24-19; or compare with the board's own first-article values)". STATUS line 16 is then true.

findings.title: Hold-up after the PA6 trip is computed from 5.3 V, above the trip window the same records define (VLOGIC about 4.8-5.2 V, PA6 0.44-0.47 V): from that window it is 0.103-0.164 ms with all ports on and 0.291-0.430 ms with the camera off / shed, not 0.157-0.182 / 0.44-0.48 ms
contradicts: M3_R10 Firmware rule 8 (lines 1014-1016), REQUIREMENTS F6 (line 60), ORDERING 8.3 (line 674), R10_VALIDATION owner row 25 (line 2164) and r10_binding_note.json firmware_obligations[43]: "the PA6 trip window is VLOGIC about 4.8-5.2 V (PA6 0.44-0.47 V)"; rule 11: PA6 = VLOGIC / 11 (board: R60 100 kOhm VLOGIC-VLOGIC_SENSE, R61 10 kOhm to GND)
REQUIREMENTS F6: the hold-up need is "the time firmware needs after the PA6 watchdog fires"; M3_R10 Power: "the hold-up must be counted from the PA6 trip, not from the battery break"

docs/ORDERING.md line 674: "From the PA6 trip (VLOGIC about 4.8-5.2 V, PA6 0.44-0.47 V; R23-POWER-01) the hold-up is only 0.157-0.182 ms with all ports on and 0.44-0.48 ms with the camera off / shed (Calculation, from 5.3 V at 300.8 uF)"

m3_design/r10_sch_check.py line 322, regenerated into r10_binding_note.json firmware_obligations[43]
evidence.calculation: Constant power, t = C (V_trip^2 - 3.8^2) / (2 P), C = 300.8 uF, P from parts_budget.json battery_break_load_W (c, all ports on: 11.249-13.064 W; d, camera off / shed: 4.295-4.650 W) (.supervisor/r25_safety/holdup.py, holdup.out). From 5.3 V: 0.157-0.182 / 0.441-0.478 ms (reproduces the records). From VLOGIC = 11 x PA6 = 4.84-5.17 V: 0.103-0.164 ms and 0.291-0.430 ms; over "4.8-5.2 V": 0.099-0.168 / 0.278-0.441 ms. The post-trip energy is 22-31 % of the break-to-3.8 V figure (34 % only at 5.3 V), not "about a third".
evidence.origin: R23-POWER-01 (round23_power.json) computed 5.3 V and 5.0 V trips (5.0 V: 0.122-0.141 ms) and stated the 4.8-5.2 V window; the records kept the 5.3 V figures beside that window.

findings.impact: The open owner question R19-REQ-07 / row 25 (how long the logic must stay up after PA6 fires, and whether C84 suffices) is answered with a post-trip hold-up overstated by up to 1.5x at the window's lower edge; against the records' own 0.2 ms shed estimate the camera-off case drops from 2.2x to 1.5x margin. No pyro or deployment effect.
findings.concrete_fix: Text, plus the rule-8 string in m3_design/r10_sch_check.py (regenerate the binding note): quote the post-trip hold-up over the stated window, e.g. "0.10-0.16 ms with all ports on and 0.29-0.43 ms with the camera off / shed (Calculation, from VLOGIC 4.84-5.17 V, PA6 0.44-0.47 V, at 300.8 uF)"; strike "the trip at about 5.3 V" in M3_R10 Power; owner rows 5 / 25 "a fifth to a third". No board change.

findings.concrete_fix: Text only: "Current R10 (`92c3ad59...`; the ports since the round 19 fix pass)".

observations: AGENTS section 2 holds on the built board: S-1 to S-9, K-actuators, K-ports and the full check_r10 contract (37 rules) pass on a probe copy; route_check --profile r10 0 failing. Gate networks by netlist: Q124 R126 220 Ohm series, R128 10 kOhm and R127 1 kOhm pull-downs, C126 220 nF gate-source; Q120 / Q121 R121 10 kOhm series, R119 || R120 100 kOhm gate-source, C120 1 uF; Q122 R122 1 kOhm, R123 2 kOhm, C123 10 nF. RAW_ACT pads are only Q121.5-9, R132.1, R134.2 and TP120 (bus after the load switch).

Q124's gate-to-drain pad gap (Q124.4 / Q124.5, F.Cu, 0.520 mm, recorded) is a single-bridge fire route with the bus enabled: gate = OUT puts Q124 in linear conduction and about 1.3-1.4 A through the match (Calculation; AON7524 VGS(th) 0.4-1.2 V, transfer curve not re-read: Inference). It is in the disclosed Q124-side class ("a failed-short Q124 can fire an enabled match"), and a pre-existing bridge reads CONT about 7 mV in the cold screen and is refused; the records state the gap but not this consequence.

U9 bypass paths give "board on with J400 open" without involving EN: U9.5-U9.6 (IN-OUT) 0.200 mm under the QFN, J1.1's kept In2 ring and the BAT_IN via (17.5,87.15) 0.251 mm from In2 RAW_PROTECTED (hole walls 0.551 mm, within JLC). Per-flight step 2 catches the symptom; its list of causes names only EN-network leaks, the J400.2 lead and the EN via open, with the same action, so not counted.

The outer-layer adjacency of 21 pyro / arming / switch / pack-live nets within 0.6 mm (109 pairs) compared on 5516eeec, 1407e850 and 92c3ad59: only BAT_ENABLE via - BAT_FAULT_N changed (0.200 -> 0.173 -> 0.200 mm), RAW_ACT - USB_OVLO 0.175 -> 0.177 mm, and ACT_GATE - BAT_SW_SOURCE left the window. Every pair with a consequence is a disclosed class (EN leak / latch, ACT_GATE or ACT_DRV to a 0 V net, Q121 / Q122 shorts, OUT to GND, R134 bypass, QSPI_IO2 / PE4, I-5).

M3_R10 Firmware "Sense plausibility (R22-POWER-02)" calls a PA6 trip that persists with the MCU running a sense fault; a genuine low pack between U9's turn-off (BAT_IN 4.29-4.80 V) and the trip (VLOGIC 4.84-5.17 V) does the same, since the AP63203 runs down to 3.8 V. The prescribed action (log and resume) is harmless in both cases; wording, not counted.

The M3_R10 CH1 and R10_VALIDATION section 1 S-8 tables (labelled 50a39de5 "updated for D-R20-05") give J400.2 In1 GND "0.250 since D-R20-05"; on 92c3ad59 it is 0.550 mm (D-R21-01; GND is exempt there). Labelled history; the re-measured sentence above the M3_R10 table is correct (1.021 / 1.050 / 2.1-2.2 mm, reproduced).
R10_VALIDATION section 1 S-8 paragraph says "on this board (`1407e850...`)" under a 92c3ad59 inventory basis; its counts (6 nets, 12 barrels) are also true on 92c3ad59.

D-R18-03's 0.5 mm floor for strong nodes beside the PC1 enable (BUZZ_OUT at LS120.2 0.520 mm, BAT_FAULT_N 0.550 mm, NRST via 0.425 mm weak) holds on the board but no check gates it; F8 sets 0.15 mm, so not a rule miss.

Owner row 21 says "pass if the longest drop-out is < 10 ms and below the 5.73 V figure" while ORDERING 8.3 says "Keep the < 10 ms single-drop-out rule"; F6 and the ORDERING C87 bullet carry the 8.2 ms / 5.96 V limit, and U9 staying on at 5.73 V is measured directly, so the pass rules agree in effect.

Per-flight list (ORDERING 8.3) against the D-R24-19 timing: opening J400 turns U9 off within about 57 ms at the slowest corner (8.4 V, C87 1.27 x, R81 +1 %, EN leakage sourcing) and the ACT_GATE decay (50 kOhm x 1 uF) takes Q120 / Q121 off within about 0.1 s, inside step 3's 1 s; step 5's fresh power-up follows the 30-130 ms turn-on; every probe position in the worksheet matches the board.
Rounding only: D-R24-02 quotes 1.042 mm (Q120 barrel to R121.2) and 0.342 mm (Q121 barrel to ACT_FET_S); pcbnew gives 1.041 and 0.341 mm.

coverage_limits: No DRC or kicad-cli run by this lens; DRC results are taken from the records (route_check, fit_check and check_r10 were run on a copy).
Inner layers were checked at the protected barrels and the BAT_IN / BAT_SW_SOURCE barrels only, not as a full plane-to-plane inventory.
No hot-plug or transient simulation; the EN and hold-up results are calculations on datasheet limits.
D402 and Q121 leakage above 25 / 55 C are not specified by the makers.
Harness faults were considered as recorded; no firmware exists and no physical test was run.
